condition.label: iliotibial-band-related lateral knee pain
condition.distinctions: ITB-related lateral knee pain differs from generic hip weakness or all lateral knee pain; no universal biomechanical cause established.

scope.stage: Chronic>=3 months in 2020pilot; 2026symptom duration not clear.

scope.exclusions: Other lateral-knee sources such as meniscal, ligament, OA or popliteus disease require differentiation.
scope.uncertainty: Research extraction only; no universal safe dose, clearance or diagnosis inferred.

integrity.method: Source record and Europe PMC REST core metadata inspected, including commentCorrectionList and firstPublicationDate; selected DOI correction/retraction web searches; no formal registry-wide audit.
integrity.result: No correction/retraction link in the inspected Europe PMC core metadata; bounded metadata check, not registry-wide clearance.

sources.population: Female recreational runners 19–45,>=15km/week, unilateral ITBS>=3 months; Noble/local tenderness; other knee disease excluded.
sources.comparator: ITB stretching vs conventional hip exercises vs progressive complex hip/core exercise.
sources.coInterventions: All avoid painful activity then gradual return; running progression after 30 min pain-free fast walk.
sources.outcomes: 8-week within-group changes across pain/LEFS, strength/balance; some between-group contrasts. Exploratory, multiple outcomes; no robust superiority conclusion or precise general effectCI.
sources.followUp: 8 weeks; no recurrence reported within that window.
sources.uncertainty: Small women-only sample, 4dropouts, short follow-up, self-report, per-protocol, multiplicity; no untreated control.
sources.harms: No recurrence during study; formal adverse-event collection not clearly reported.
sources.limitations: Small women-only sample, 4dropouts, short follow-up, self-report, per-protocol, multiplicity; no untreated control.

protocol.execution: Progresses modified side plank/clamshell, side-lying abduction to band walks, hip hike to single-leg squat, bridge variants.
protocol.dose: Examples Table 2: modified side plank 30sx 2 week 1; abduction 10x 2 week 1 to 10x 3 week 2; clam+modified plank 10x 2 light band week 3 to 15x 3 week 4; single-leg squat 10x 2 week 3 to 12x 3 week 4.
protocol.supervision: Designed by kinesiologist/strength coach; measurement visits; continuous-session supervision not specified.
protocol.progression: Weekly Table 2 complexity progression; pain-free 30 min fast walk before run intervals.
protocol.stoppingRules: Avoid painful activities until controlled; no numeric pain/load cap.

sources.population: Adult runners, mostly 18–35, Noble or Ober positive, NPRS>5, running>=5/week; other pathology/surgery excluded.
sources.comparator: Hip/knee strengthening vs deep friction/stretch/mobilization/foam-roll manual therapy.
sources.coInterventions: Usual running if tolerable; no new terrain/intensity/footwear or analgesics; weekly logs.
sources.outcomes: Table 4 NPRS manual 8.88→8.12, strength 8.41→2.88; LEFS 43.94→50.24 vs 41.12→57.33. Table 5 pooled pain figures conflict with Table 4 and baseline imbalance p.04. No trustworthy adjusted effect/CI supplied.
sources.uncertainty: Small single-center pilot; diagnosis includes Ober alone; statistical-table inconsistencies; baseline pain imbalance; no long-term or no-treatment comparator. Very low confidence.
sources.harms: Adverse-event reporting not identified; no long-term recurrence measure.
sources.limitations: Small single-center pilot; diagnosis includes Ober alone; statistical-table inconsistencies; baseline pain imbalance; no long-term or no-treatment comparator. Very low confidence.

protocol.execution: Modified side plank/clamshell, band walks, single-leg squat/bridges, then lunges, Bulgarian split squat, hip thrust.
protocol.dose: Table 2 examples: week 1 modifiedplank 2x 15(5 s); week 2 squat 2x 12–15(2 s); week 5 Bulgarian 2x 12–15; week 6 3x 15–20.
protocol.frequency: 5/week for 6 weeks; 30 s interset, 1 min between exercises.
protocol.supervision: Clinical setting; standard initial instructions; qualifications/session monitoring not fully specified.
protocol.progression: Table 2 weekly sets/reps/complexity; external load not quantified.
protocol.stoppingRules: Tolerable running without quantified cutoff; no explicit exercise stopping algorithm.

findings.statement: McKay 24 analyzed participants showed within-group improvements and some between-group contrasts; small per-protocol pilot with multiple outcomes cannot establish robust regimen superiority.
findings.applicability: Female recreational runners 19–45,>=15km/week, unilateral ITBS>=3 months; Noble/local tenderness; other knee disease excluded.
findings.limitations: 8 weeks, women-only, no untreated group; confidence low.

findings.statement: McKay instructed avoidance of painful activities until controlled, then gradual reintroduction; running intervals began after 30 min pain-free fast walking.
findings.applicability: Participants in this chronic female-runner pilot.
findings.limitations: Advice not separately randomized; no universal gym-load cap or pain cutoff.

findings.statement: Table 4 NPRS manual 8.88→8.12, strength 8.41→2.88; LEFS 43.94→50.24 vs 41.12→57.33. Table 5 pooled pain figures conflict with Table 4 and baseline imbalance p.04. No trustworthy adjusted effect/CI supplied.
findings.applicability: Adult runners, mostly 18–35, Noble or Ober positive, NPRS>5, running>=5/week; other pathology/surgery excluded.
findings.limitations: Low confidence; no numerical rule from inconsistent outcome tables.

exerciseMappings.matchRationale: Catalog side-plank supports forearm/foot and duration; banded-clamshell is separate dynamic hip work. Neither metadata establishes this combined supported-knee variant; retain separate PNG identity if commissioned.
Catalog side-lying-hip-abduction has matching position/type but no study-specific execution verification. No PNG-frame review was performed, so direct equivalence remains unresolved.

proposedRules.statement: Retain progressive hip/core exercise variants as clinical-content research candidates; do not declare the experimental program superior or copy all weekly progressions into an ordinary split.

proposedRules.statement: Candidate ordinary-workout implication: identify and modify symptom-provoking activities with gradual return; keep a clinician-set response plan instead of a blanket squat or running ban.
